fields.label: Authority Types
fields.description: V2 spec section 12: execution/decision/approval/assignment are kept as four separate grants, not one permission flag.

fields.label: Execution Authority
fields.description: May perform an authorized action. In practice this is redundant with a non-empty allowed_semantic_tools list; kept explicit for the formal model and so a policy can be defined with zero execution authority (observer-only) without clearing the tool list.

fields.label: Decision Authority
fields.description: May choose which course of action to take (e.g. which supplier) rather than following a prescribed script. Not yet enforced at runtime -- DeterministicProvider always exercises judgment -- but recorded so a future prescribed-process provider can check it.

fields.label: Assignment Authority
fields.description: May allocate work to other actors. Ties into EORL Task Assignment; no policy in this system grants it yet since every architecture built so far has exactly one candidate per slot.

fields.label: May Approve
fields.description: This is the Approval Authority grant (V2 section 12 type 3).

fields.label: Soft Rules (V2 section 13)
fields.description: Hard constraints (above) reject the action outright. A soft rule is logged but never blocks execution -- violating it is an observable organizational event, not a firewall denial.

fields.label: Large-Order Soft Threshold (Qty)
fields.description: If set, a create_purchase_order call with qty above this value is still allowed, but logs a soft_rule_violation event (e.g. 'large purchases should have manager pre-approval'). Milestone scope: one concrete soft rule, not a general rule DSL.
